title: What a Member's Allowance Card Meets Against a Restated Liability
content:
A member holding one of the Optional Supplemental Benefit Riders may also hold a card under the Supplemental Benefit Allowance Programmes. Where such a card stands on the member's records, part of what is left owing on a line put right may be met from it.

## The rule

1. Where the member holds an allowance card programme that makes dental, vision and hearing costs eligible and the balance standing on it is above the most one card transaction may carry, the card meets the most one card transaction may carry on that programme.
2. Where the member holds such a programme and the balance standing on it is not above that figure, the card meets the balance standing on the card.
3. Otherwise the card meets nothing of what is left.

## What is read from the member's card records

Two things are read from the member's Supplemental Benefit Allowance Programmes records: whether the card programme held makes dental, vision and hearing costs eligible, and the balance standing on the card. The most one card transaction may carry is a term of the card programme the member holds.

## Condition and amount met

| The card programme held | The balance standing on the card | What the card meets |
|---|---|---|
| Makes dental, vision and hearing costs eligible | Above the most one card transaction may carry | The most one card transaction may carry |
| Makes dental, vision and hearing costs eligible | At or below that figure | The balance standing on the card |
| Does not make those costs eligible, or no such programme is held | Any | Nothing |

## Worked on hypothetical inputs

Take a card programme making dental, vision and hearing costs eligible whose transaction ceiling is 200.00 USD.

- A balance of 350.00 USD stands above that ceiling: the card meets 200.00 USD.
- A balance of 120.00 USD does not stand above it: the card meets 120.00 USD.
- A balance of 200.00 USD does not stand above it: the card meets the whole 200.00 USD, which comes to the same either way.
- Where the programme held does not make dental, vision and hearing costs eligible, the card meets nothing whatever balance stands on it.
